1.body: A lit window on a dark street. You're inside, eating.

2.title: The bite

1.title: What happens to my photo?
1.body: It is used only to make your video and deleted about 24 hours after upload. We never use photos or videos to train AI. Your videos stay in your private library.

2.title: Can I see the video before I pay?
2.body: No. Each video costs credits, from {price} for one. If the render fails, the credits come back to your balance.

3.title: What if my video fails?
3.body: The credits come back to your balance automatically, and you can try again. You don't need to contact us. If a photo is refused, try a different one; you don't lose credits for it.

4.title: What is the window peeper trend?
4.body: It's a staged comedy bit on TikTok. A camera creeps up to one lit window in a dark building at night. The person inside is eating, notices the camera, freezes, stares straight into the lens for too long, then pulls the curtain shut.

5.title: Is there a window peeper filter or CapCut template?
5.body: You don't need one. A filter can't film a night building and push in on a window, and a CapCut template pastes your face into someone else's footage. This site makes a new video of the person in your photo, in your own outfit, in the browser.

6.title: Which photos work best?
6.body: A photo of yourself, waist up, facing the camera, in good light, with nothing covering the face. You must be 18 or older. Photos of other people, children or public figures aren't allowed. JPG, PNG or WebP, up to {size} MB.

7.title: How long does it take?
7.body: A Standard video is usually ready in about 3 minutes, a Pro video in about 6. Keep the page open and it plays there; if you leave, it still finishes in your video library.

8.title: Is WindowPeeper safe? What can it make?
8.body: Every video is one of six fixed comedy scenes of you eating at night, fully clothed and PG-rated; there are no prompts to write. It never makes nude, sexual or intimate content, and it must not be used to make intimate images of anyone or videos of real people without their consent. That's why you may only upload a photo of yourself, 18 or older. Photos are deleted about 24 hours after upload and never used to train AI. Report misuse to {email}.

9.title: How do you use my Google data?
9.body: Sign in with Google only creates your account. We get your name, email address and profile picture, and nothing else. We don't access your Google Photos, Drive or any other Google data. We never sell it, and we share your email only with the services that run the site, such as email delivery and checkout.

how-to-make-window-peeper-video.metaTitle: How to Make the Window Peeper Video
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.metaDescription: Turn one photo into a window peeper trend video: pick a photo, choose Standard or Pro, sign in, pay if needed, then download and post it to TikTok.
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.nav: How to make a window peeper video
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.title: How to make a window peeper video
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.tagline: One photo, six steps, one stare.
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.lead: You need one photo and a few minutes. This guide walks through each step on the generator, what it costs, and how to get a good result.

text.1: You need a photo, an email address or a Google account to sign in, and enough credits for one video. Credit packs are one-time payments, not a subscription, and credits never expire.

1.title: Pick a photo
1.body: Open the <generator>generator on the home page</generator> and choose a photo of yourself, waist up, facing the camera, in good light. You must be 18 or older. It must be a JPEG, PNG or WebP up to {size} MB, from {min, number} to {maxSide, number} pixels on each side.

2.title: Confirm it's OK to use
2.body: Tick the box under the scenes to confirm the photo is of you and that you're 18 or older. Without it, the button stays off.

3.title: Choose Standard or Pro
3.body: Standard costs {credits} credits and is 720p. Pro costs {proCredits} credits and is 1080p. Both make the scene you pick, about 14 seconds long, with music.

4.title: Sign in
4.body: Press Make my video. If you aren't signed in, sign in with an email link or Google in the window that opens. Your photo stays picked while you do.

5.title: Pay if you need credits
5.body: If your balance is short, the generator offers the packs: {packs}. After checkout you come back to the page, and the video starts as soon as the credits arrive.

6.title: Wait, then download and post
6.body: A video usually takes a few minutes. Keep the page open, and it plays there when it's ready. Download saves the MP4. Post it to TikTok with #windowpeeper, and add the trending sound in the app if you want it.

list.1: One person only. The scene has one person at the table.
list.2: Waist up, facing the camera, with nothing covering the face.
list.3: Wear what you want in the video. The outfit comes from the photo.
list.4: Use even light. Dark or backlit photos give a blurry face.
list.5: Skip heavy filters, stickers and text on the photo.

text.1: If a video fails, or doesn't finish within 24 hours, its credits go back to your balance automatically. You don't need to contact us. If a photo is refused, try a different one; you don't lose credits for it.
text.2: If you leave the page, the video still finishes. It appears in your video library, and we email you when it's ready. For anything else, email <email></email>.

text.1: Your photo is used only to make your video, and it is deleted about 24 hours after upload. The finished video stays in your library until you delete your account. The <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> has the details.
text.2: Only upload photos of yourself, and only if you're 18 or older. No photos of other people, children or public figures, and nothing meant to deceive, harass or frighten anyone. The trend is a joke about being watched; keep it one.

window-peeper-trend.metaDescription: The window peeper trend explained: a camera creeps up to a lit window at night, and the person inside freezes mid-bite, stares and closes the curtain.
window-peeper-trend.nav: What is the window peeper trend?
window-peeper-trend.title: What is the window peeper trend?
window-peeper-trend.tagline: A creepy setup with a silly payoff.
window-peeper-trend.lead: The window peeper trend is a staged comedy bit on TikTok, Reels and Shorts. It looks like a horror clip for a few seconds, then turns into a joke about being caught eating.

1.title: The approach
1.body: A camera at night slowly pushes in on a dark apartment building, toward the one window that's lit.

2.title: The bite
2.body: Through the glass, someone sits at a table and eats: a burger, noodles, a slice of pizza. They don't know they're being filmed.

3.title: The freeze
3.body: Mid-bite, they notice the camera and stop chewing.

4.title: The stare
4.body: They look straight into the lens, without blinking, for longer than is comfortable. This is the joke.

5.title: The curtain
5.body: They stand up and yank the curtain shut. The window glows behind it, and the clip ends.

list.1: It flips the horror setup: the person being watched catches the watcher, and wins.
list.2: The stare runs a beat too long, which makes it awkward rather than scary.
list.3: Eating is ordinary and a little embarrassing to be caught doing, so anyone can play the part.
list.4: The whole bit fits in about 14 seconds, a vertical frame and one sound, so it's easy to remix.

text.1: Clips in this format circulate on TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. We don't know who posted the first one, so we don't name an origin, a date or a sound we can't check. The format is the same across versions: the night building, the lit window, the meal, the stare and the curtain.

You don't need a building, a long lens or a second person. Upload a photo of yourself to the <generator>generator on the home page</generator>, pick a scene, and you get a new 14-second vertical video of you in the window, with music. A Standard video costs {credits} credits, from {price}.
text.2: The <howto>step-by-step guide</howto> covers the photo, the scenes, pricing and posting. Six scenes change the meal and the ending: a burger, midnight noodles, a pizza slice, a small wave instead of the curtain, rain on the glass, and a dinner for two where only you notice the camera.

text.1: The trend is about pretending to be watched. Don't film real people through their windows, and don't make a video of someone else. On this site you may only upload a photo of yourself, and only if you're 18 or older. Every scene is fixed and PG-rated; there are no prompts to write. The <terms>Terms</terms> have the full rules.

window-peeper-capcut-template.metaTitle: Window Peeper CapCut Template vs AI
window-peeper-capcut-template.metaDescription: How a window peeper CapCut template works, why it may not show up for you, and how it compares with making the video from one photo with AI.
window-peeper-capcut-template.title: Window peeper CapCut template
window-peeper-capcut-template.tagline: Template or one photo: which one fits you.
window-peeper-capcut-template.lead: Searching for a window peeper CapCut template? Here's how templates work, what to try when one won't open, and when making the video from one photo is the easier route.

text.1: A CapCut template is someone else's edit with empty slots. You fill the slots with your own clips or photos, and CapCut keeps the cuts, effects and sound. For this trend, that means you still need footage that fits each slot.

1.title: Search in CapCut
1.body: Open the CapCut app and search for "window peeper". Templates come and go, and some only show up in certain regions, so we don't link one here.

2.title: Check the preview
2.body: Play the preview and count the slots. Make sure it's the night window, the stare and the curtain, not a different trend with a similar name.

3.title: Add your media
3.body: Tap Use template and fill each slot with clips or photos that match it.

4.title: Export and post
4.body: Export the video and post it. Add the trending sound in the app if the template doesn't carry it.

list.1: Update the CapCut app; old versions hide newer templates.
list.2: Search other names for the trend, such as "window stare" or "curtain close".
list.3: Templates can be limited by region or removed by their creator. If it's gone, it's gone.
list.4: Open a window peeper clip in TikTok and use its sound or template link from there.

compare.title: Template or AI from one photo?

list.1: What you need: a template needs clips that fit its slots. This site needs one photo of yourself.
list.2: What you get: a template puts your media into its edit. Here you get a new 14-second video of you in the window, eating, staring and closing the curtain, with original music.
list.3: Control: a template lets you edit the cuts in CapCut. Here you pick one of six fixed scenes; there are no prompts to write.
list.4: Cost: CapCut's own terms apply to templates. Here a Standard video costs {credits} credits, from {price}, and a failed video gives its credits back.

more.1: Want the exact edit someone else made? Use the template. Want the trend starring you without filming anything? Use the <generator>generator on the home page</generator>, or read <howto>how to make a window peeper video</howto> first.

Footer.blurb: An independent tool. Not affiliated with TikTok, CapCut or the creators of the original clip.
